authoredSolutions.51: With \(\alpha+\beta=1,\ \alpha\beta=p\) and \(\gamma+\delta=4,\ \gamma\delta=q\). Taking the four terms in G.P. as \(a,ar,ar^2,ar^3\): \(a(1+r)=1\) and \(ar^2(1+r)=4\Rightarrow r^2=4\). For integer \(p,q\) take \(r=-2,\ a=-1\), giving \(p=a^2r=-2,\ q=a^2r^5=-32\). Hence \(|p+q|=34\).
authoredSolutions.53: Expanding the determinant along the first column gives \(f(n)=3n(2k+1)(k^2+5k+1)+2n^2(27k^2+9k-1)-42n^3(2k+1)\). Summing \(n=1\) to \(k\) and testing \(k=3\): \(3150+7532-10584=98\). Hence \(k=3\).
authoredSolutions.54: The columns of \(M\) are the given images: \(M=\begin{pmatrix}1&0&-1\\2&1&1\\3&2&1\end{pmatrix}\). Solving \(x-z=1,\ 2x+y+z=7,\ 3x+2y+z=11\) gives \(z=1,\ x=2,\ y=2\) (check: \(M(2,2,1)^T=(1,7,11)^T\)). Thus \(x+y+z=5\).
authoredSolutions.55: Using \(1+4r^4=(2r^2-2r+1)(2r^2+2r+1)\), \(\frac{r}{1+4r^4}=\frac14\left(\frac{1}{2r^2-2r+1}-\frac{1}{2r^2+2r+1}\right)\), which telescopes. The sum \(=\frac14\left(1-\frac{1}{221}\right)=\frac{55}{221}\). So \(m+n=276\).
authoredSolutions.59: Enumerate colour splits \((b,y,r)\), each \(\ge2\), summing to 8, and add \(\binom{5}{b}\binom{6}{y}\binom{4}{r}\): \(150+800+900+600+1200+450=4100\).
authoredSolutions.60: Mean \(=\frac{\sum k(k-1)\binom{n}{k}}{2^n}=\frac{n(n-1)2^{n-2}}{2^n}=\frac{n(n-1)}{4}=60\Rightarrow n=16\). Total frequency \(2^{16}\); \(\sum_{k=0}^{7}\binom{16}{k}=26333<2^{15}\), so the median falls at \(k=8\), value \(8\cdot7=56\).
authoredSolutions.61: Vertex \(P=(3,3)\). For the circle (centre \((1,2)\), \(r^2=2\)), the power of \(P\) is \(PR\cdot PS=|PC|^2-r^2=5-2=3\). With \(|PC|=\sqrt5\), \(PR+PS=2\sqrt5\cos\theta\), maximised for a line through the centre, giving \((PR+PS)^2=20\).
authoredSolutions.62: For \(y^2=8x\), \(A=(-2,0)\), focus \((2,0)\). A point \((2t^2,4t)\) with slope \(\frac{2t}{t^2+1}=\frac35\) gives \(t=3\) (since \(\alpha>1\)), so \(B=(18,12)\); the focal-chord partner is \(C=(2/9,-4/3)\). authoredSolutions.63: From \(6e^2-11e+3=0\), \(e=\frac32\) (taking \(e>1\)). Distance between foci \(2c=9\Rightarrow c=\frac92\), so \(a=\frac{c}{e}=3\) and \(b^2=c^2-a^2=\frac{45}{4}\). Latus rectum \(=\frac{2b^2}{a}=\frac{15}{2}\).
authoredSolutions.64: The foot of the perpendicular from \(R(1,2,3)\) to the line is \(M=(1,5,0)\) (at parameter \(t=\tfrac12\)). Since \(P,Q\) are symmetric about \(M\), \(P+Q=2M\), so the centroid \(=\frac{2M+R}{3}=(1,4,1)\). Hence \(\alpha+\beta+\gamma=6\).
authoredSolutions.65: The foot of the perpendicular from \((1,2,7)\) to the line is \((2,3,6)\), so its image is \((3,4,5)\). Then \((a-3)^2+(2-4)^2+0=16\Rightarrow(a-3)^2=12\), so \(a=3\pm2\sqrt3\) and the sum \(=6\).
authoredSolutions.66: \(\overrightarrow{OR}=\frac15\vec a\) and \(\overrightarrow{RM}=\frac15\vec b\), so \(\overrightarrow{OM}=\frac15\vec a+\frac15\vec b\). Then \(\overrightarrow{PM}=\overrightarrow{OM}-\vec a=\frac15\vec b-\frac45\vec a=\frac15(\vec b-4\vec a)\).
authoredSolutions.67: \(f(x)=\lim_{y\to0}\frac{(1-\cos xy)\tan xy}{y^3}=\lim_{y\to0}\frac{\frac{x^2y^2}{2}\cdot xy}{y^3}=\frac{x^3}{2}\). Solving \(\frac{x^3}{2}=\sin x\): \(x=0\) is a root, and by odd symmetry there is one positive and one negative root (near \(\pm1.24\)). Hence there are 3 solutions.
authoredSolutions.68: The A.P. gives \(2f(a)=(2^{1-a}+2^{1+a})+(3^a+3^{-a})\), so \(f(a)=(2^a+2^{-a})+\tfrac12(3^a+3^{-a})\), minimised at \(a=0\): \(\alpha=3\). With \(u=e^{2x}\), \(\int\frac{dx}{e^{2x}-e^{-2x}}=\frac14\ln\frac{u-1}{u+1}\). From \(x=\ln2\ (u=4)\) to \(x=\ln3\ (u=9)\): \(\frac14\left(\ln\frac{8}{10}-\ln\frac35\right)=\frac14\ln\frac43\).
authoredSolutions.69: Differentiating, \(f'(x)=f(x)-\ln x+\frac1x\), i.e. \(f'-f=-\ln x+\frac1x\). A particular solution is \(\ln x\), so \(f(x)=\ln x+Ce^x\); from \(f(1)=e\), \(C=1\), giving \(f(x)=\ln x+e^x\). Then \(f(1)=e\) and \(f(e)=1+e^e\).
authoredSolutions.71: Both \(a_1+b_2\) and \(a_2+b_1\) range over the multiset \(\{3,4,6,7,9,9,10,12,15\}\). Counting ordered pairs \((s,t)\) with \(s\mid t\): \(6+2+2+1+2+2+1+1+1=18\).
authoredSolutions.72: The two rays are \(x=-1\) and \(y=-1\), meeting the mirror \(x+2y=1\) at \((-1,1)\) and \((3,-1)\). Reflecting the incident directions about the normal \((1,2)\) gives reflected rays \(4x+3y=9\) and \(-3x+4y=7\). Thus \((a,b,c,d)=(4,3,-3,4)\) and \(ad+bc=16-9=7\).
authoredSolutions.73: Product-to-sum reduces the equation to \(\cos\frac{3\theta}{2}=\cos\frac{21\theta}{2}\), giving \(\theta=\frac{2n\pi}{9}\) (9 values) or \(\theta=\frac{n\pi}{6}\) (13 values) in \([-\pi,\pi]\), with 3 common values. Hence \(n(S)=9+13-3=19\).
authoredSolutions.74: Replacing \(x\to\frac\pi2-x\) and solving the pair gives \(f(x)=\frac{3\cos x-\sin x}{8}\), with maximum \(\alpha=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{8}\), so \(\alpha^2=\frac{5}{32}\). The area between \(x^2\) and \(\beta x^3\) is \(\frac{1}{12\beta^3}=\frac{5}{32}\Rightarrow\beta^3=\frac{8}{15}\), hence \(30\beta^3=16\).
authoredSolutions.75: Rewriting: \(\frac{dy}{dx}+(\tan x)y=\sec^3x(\tan x)^{-1/2}\), with integrating factor \(\sec x\). Then \(y\sec x=2\sqrt{\tan x}+\frac25(\tan x)^{5/2}+C\); \(y(\pi/4)=\frac{6\sqrt2}{5}\Rightarrow C=0\). At \(x=\pi/3\), \(y=\frac85\cdot3^{1/4}=\frac45\alpha\Rightarrow\alpha=2\cdot3^{1/4}\), so \(\alpha^4=48\).
